label: How Much Does a Website Cost in the UK?
title: How Much Does a Website Cost in the UK? (2026 Guide)
description: How much does a website cost in the UK? Small business website prices explained: DIY builders vs web designers vs agencies, monthly costs and what affects price.
h1: How much does a website cost in the UK?
intro: The honest answer is that it depends on who builds it and what it needs to do. This guide explains the main options for a small business, what drives the price, and the ongoing costs to budget for.
highlights: A basic small business website from a small studio: from around £199
Multi-page business websites: typically a few hundred pounds upwards
Agency websites: often £5,000 or more
Ongoing costs: domain name, hosting and any monthly services

sections.title: Option 1: Build it yourself
sections.text: DIY website builders charge a monthly subscription and you do the design, writing and setup. It can be the cheapest upfront, but it costs time, the monthly fees add up year after year, and the result often looks like a template. It suits businesses that have the time and enjoy doing it themselves.

sections.title: Option 2: A freelancer or small studio
sections.text: A small studio builds a custom website for a one-off price, usually with far lower overheads than an agency. For most small businesses this is the best value: a professional design without agency fees. At Blueframe Digital, a Website Starter begins at £199 and a multi-page Business Website at £399.

sections.title: Option 3: A digital agency
sections.text: Agencies bring larger teams, strategy workshops and account management, which is reflected in the price. Small business websites from agencies often cost £5,000 or more. That can make sense for large or complex projects, but it's more than most local businesses need.

sections.title: What affects the price of a website?
sections.text: The number of pages, whether the design is custom, who writes the content, features such as galleries, booking systems, memberships or online stores, integrations with other tools, and how much support you want after launch. A simple brochure website costs far less than an online store or a booking platform.

sections.title: Monthly and yearly running costs
sections.text: Every website needs a domain name, which is renewed each year, and hosting to keep it online. Some businesses also pay monthly for an online store platform, email, or services like social media management. Ask for these costs upfront so there are no surprises. With us, hosting and domains are discussed before you commit, and online stores start from £15 a month.

sections.title: So what should a small business pay?
sections.text: For most small and local businesses, a professional website from a small studio in the region of a few hundred pounds is enough to look established and win enquiries. Spend more when you need more pages, more features or ongoing help, not just to pay for agency overheads.

faqs.q: How much does a basic website cost in the UK?
faqs.a: A basic small business website from a small studio can start from around £199. Agencies typically charge much more. DIY builders are cheaper upfront but have ongoing monthly fees and take your time.

faqs.q: How much does a website cost per month in the UK?
faqs.a: A one-off website still has running costs: an annual domain renewal and hosting. Online stores and other platforms usually add a monthly fee. Our online stores start from £15 a month.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to use Wix or Squarespace?
faqs.a: Website builders can be cheaper upfront, but you pay a subscription for as long as the site is live and you build it yourself. A professionally built website can work out better value over a few years and usually looks and performs better.

faqs.q: Why do agencies charge so much more?
faqs.a: Agencies have larger teams, offices and account managers, and that overhead is built into their prices. Small studios can deliver professional results for small businesses at a fraction of the cost.
